results.summary: This project is a self-contained hardware authentication engine that generates, stores and verifies a 4-digit (16-bit) one-time password using a 16-bit LFSR and an FSM. The FSM controls authentication, retry and timeout operations, and the result is shown on seven-segment displays as unlocked, locked or expired. It is tested by latching an OTP, entering four digits with user_in and user_latch, and observing the displayed result. The design is implemented in Verilog and is described as lightweight and Tiny Tapeout friendly, with observable outputs on FPGA using LEDs and seven-segment displays.

results.summary: This project implements a 3-bit R-2R DAC together with a ring oscillator, based on an analog design by Harald Pretl and Jakob Ratschenberger for Tiny Tapeout 5. The DAC output voltage is nominally 1.8 V divided by 8 times the 3-bit input value, and the ring oscillator provides a rail-to-rail clock output at about 500 kHz. It is tested by applying digital bits to inputs 0-2 and measuring the analog output with a voltmeter or oscilloscope. The design is an analog mixed-signal circuit with a nominal 1.8 V supply.
